title: Minimax Rates for Mean Subject-Quantile Treatment Contrasts under a Count-Tail Condition
banked_reason: The delivered frontier concerns one mixing-CDF contrast in a binary latent experiment with a fixed polynomial count law; it does not characterize general subject-distribution quantiles or optimal allocation under a measurement budget.
gap_reasons: The delivered frontier concerns one mixing-CDF contrast in a binary latent experiment with a fixed polynomial count law; it does not characterize general subject-distribution quantiles or optimal allocation under a measurement budget.
Efficient coverage is pointwise at strictly positive densities and requires infinite expected readings, substantially restricting its prospective design relevance.

Certified numerical termination establishes an observable construction, but the package demonstrates neither manageable computational cost nor useful finite-sample performance near the information boundary.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 completed and maximized the full published Holder-class sharp MSE frontier, including the critical logarithm and feasible pointwise efficient inference at strictly positive densities. The math referee passed with zero findings and all eleven cited sources verified, but the cold general referee graded the specialized experiment subfield (score ceiling 7 against field floor 7.4) with no same-scope improvement directive. Two independent terminal judgments confirmed that crossing the field floor requires a broader substantive deliverable; the run stopped before F1 and no Lean formalization was produced.
tldr: Mean subject medians compare latent subject distributions across randomized arms. In this binary latent experiment, unbounded counts identify the causal contrast. The sharp minimax mean squared error on the published radius-\(10\) full-interval class \(\mathcal G_s^2\) is \(n^{-1}\) for \(\beta<1/2\), \((\log n)/n\) for \(\beta=1/2\), and \(n^{-(2s+2)/(2s+2\beta+1)}\) for \(\beta>1/2\). One observable filtered statistic attains these orders, and exact-likelihood alternatives prove matching lower bounds on the same class. At every strictly positive smooth density pair, finite-variance regular Gaussian inference exists exactly when \(\beta<1/2\). Complete observable controls compute the actual-law efficient variance; the canonical pilot ridge theorem proves its attainment, consistent standard errors, local-path regularity and pointwise coverage using only second moments. Finite expected readings require \(\beta>1\), excluding this finite-information regime. The calibrated positive subclass \(\mathcal H_s\) supplies prospective examples and lower witnesses. This is a prospective count-design benchmark rather than an empirical reanalysis of the clinical application.
gap: Lee, Baćak, and Kennedy give heterogeneous-trial density bounds, while Peng et al. transfer an available asymptotic linear representation to a mean subject quantile. Neither cited theorem determines threshold-functional precision when one public random count law remains fixed with sample size. Trabs supplies the abstract information criterion; its concrete weighted inverse still has to be computed.
fill: A single observable filtered Legendre statistic is paired with exact-likelihood lower alternatives in the identical numerical benchmark class. Complete conditional-mean-zero controls specify finite weighted projection systems and a convergent efficient-variance series at every strictly positive density pair. Pilot regularization must make that series operational without knowing a lower-density constant, and the information result must answer whether finite expected readings are compatible with regular Gaussian inference.
